s: The Satavahanas were
Which Vishnukundin ruler had transferred the capital from Amarapuri to Denduluru?
x:
The Vishnukundins emerged as an important dynasty in the Deccan after the decline of the Ikshvakus and the Salankayanas. Their early capital was Amarapuri (identified with Amaravati region). As the kingdom expanded towards the coastal Andhra region, Madhavavarma II shifted the capital to Denduluru (near present-day Eluru in West Godavari district). This strategic shift enabled better control over the fertile Vengi region and facilitated administration of the eastern coastal territories. Madhavavarma II was the most powerful ruler of the dynasty. He assumed the title Janasraya, performed several Vedic sacrifices such as the Ashvamedha, and greatly expanded the kingdom. Why the other options are incorrect:
Option (1): Vikramendravarma – He was an important Vishnukundin ruler but is not credited with shifting the capital to Denduluru.
Option (3): Govindavarma – Founder of the Vishnukundin dynasty. During his reign, the capital remained at Amarapuri.
Option (4): Manchana Bhattaraka – A later ruler who ruled during the declining phase of the dynasty and did not shift the capital.
Exam Note:
• Founder – Govindavarma
• Greatest ruler – Madhavavarma II (Janasraya)
• Early Capital – Amarapuri
• Later Capital – Denduluru

The Vishnukundins had earlier capitals at Indrapalanagara and Vishnukundapuram, showing the centre moved repeatedly during their 5th- 6th century rule.

s: Undavalli Caves are associated with
x:
The Undavalli Caves, situated near Vijayawada on the banks of the Krishna River, are among the finest examples of rock-cut architecture in Andhra Pradesh. These caves were excavated during the Vishnukundin period (5th–6th Century CE). Although they were originally developed as Buddhist monastic caves, they were later converted into Hindu cave temples. The most striking feature of the caves is the monolithic reclining image of Lord Vishnu (Anantasayana Vishnu) carved from a single block of granite. The caves consist of four storeys, displaying remarkable rock-cut architectural skill and reflecting the transition from Buddhist to Hindu religious traditions. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).
Exam Note:
• Location – Near Vijayawada
• Period – Vishnukundins
• Famous Sculpture – Reclining Vishnu (Anantasayana)
• Type – Rock-cut cave temple

s: Brahmanical cave temples of Mogalrajapuram and Undavalli are assigned to
x: The rock-cut Brahmanical cave temples at Mogalrajapuram and Undavalli, near Vijayawada, are architecturally and historically attributed to the Vishnukundin dynasty, reflecting their patronage of Hindu (particularly Vaishnavite) cave architecture.

s: Undavally caves are associated with:
x: The Undavalli caves near Vijayawada are rock-cut cave temples primarily attributed to Vishnukundin dynasty patronage (5th-6th century CE), including a notable multi-storied cave with a large reclining Vishnu sculpture, showing early Deccan cavearchitecture traditions.

s: Who owns the Brahmin style caves in Moghalrajapuram and Undavalli?
x:
The rock-cut cave temples at Moghalrajapuram and Undavalli are generally attributed to the Vishnukundins, who ruled large parts of Andhra Pradesh during the 5th and 6th centuries CE. These caves represent some of the earliest examples of Brahmanical rock-cut architecture in Andhra. They contain sculptures of Shiva, Vishnu and other Hindu deities, indicating the growing influence of Hinduism during the Vishnukundin period. The Undavalli Caves are particularly famous for the massive monolithic image of Anantasayana Vishnu, while the Moghalrajapuram Caves contain important Shaivite sculptures. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Dynasty – Vishnukundins
• Important Caves – Undavalli and Moghalrajapuram
• Religion – Brahmanical (Hindu)
